variants.title: Give each part its job
variants.context: Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) is a vocabulary-learning algorithm that repeatedly replaces the most frequent adjacent symbol pair with one new symbol. In tokenization, those learned symbols become reusable subword pieces such as low, ing, or _user.
variants.prompt: Match each part to its responsibility.

pairs.label: Characters or bytes
pairs.detail: Any input can fall back to small symbols, but common words and identifiers become long sequences.
pairs.explanation: Any input can fall back to small symbols, but common words and identifiers become long sequences. That consumes context and repeats work in every transformer layer.

pairs.label: Whole words
pairs.detail: Frequent words can use one ID, but spelling variants, names, code, and new terms create an unbounded vocabulary or collapse into an unknown token.
pairs.explanation: Frequent words can use one ID, but spelling variants, names, code, and new terms create an unbounded vocabulary or collapse into an unknown token.

pairs.label: BPE subwords
pairs.detail: Frequent adjacent pieces earn compact tokens.
pairs.explanation: Frequent adjacent pieces earn compact tokens. Rare text remains representable from smaller symbols, assuming the base alphabet or byte fallback covers the input.

pairs.label: Initialize symbols
pairs.detail: Normalize and pre-tokenize the corpus, split each word into characters or bytes, and retain a word-ending marker such as </w>.

pairs.label: Count adjacent pairs
pairs.detail: Count pairs inside every current token sequence and multiply by each sequence's corpus frequency.
pairs.explanation: Count pairs inside every current token sequence and multiply by each sequence's corpus frequency.

pairs.label: Merge the winner
pairs.detail: Choose the highest-frequency eligible pair, replace every non-overlapping occurrence, and append the result to the vocabulary.

pairs.label: Repeat to budget
pairs.detail: Recount from the new segmentation until the vocabulary budget or minimum-frequency rule stops training.

pairs.label: Word-level BPE
pairs.detail: Training starts from characters within pre-tokenized words and commonly uses an end-of-word marker.
pairs.explanation: Training starts from characters within pre-tokenized words and commonly uses an end-of-word marker. The pre-tokenizer decides which cross-boundary pairs are impossible.

pairs.label: Byte-level BPE
pairs.detail: Input bytes are mapped to a reversible visible alphabet before merges.
pairs.explanation: Input bytes are mapped to a reversible visible alphabet before merges. This avoids a global unknown token, but unusual Unicode text can expand into several byte-derived pieces.

pairs.label: SentencePiece BPE
pairs.detail: SentencePiece learns over a representation that includes whitespace markers and does not require a separate language-specific word tokenizer.
pairs.explanation: SentencePiece learns over a representation that includes whitespace markers and does not require a separate language-specific word tokenizer. Its normalization is still an explicit contract.

variants.hint:

Byte-level BPE: Input bytes are mapped to a reversible visible alphabet before merges.

SentencePiece BPE: SentencePiece learns over a representation that includes whitespace markers and does not require a separate language-specific word tokenizer.

pairs.label: Slice expansion
pairs.detail: An underrepresented language, code style, or domain produces many more tokens than the average, raising truncation and latency for that slice.
pairs.explanation: An underrepresented language, code style, or domain produces many more tokens than the average, raising truncation and latency for that slice.

pairs.label: Normalization drift
pairs.detail: Training and serving disagree about case, Unicode composition, whitespace, or control characters, so familiar text reaches different merges.
pairs.explanation: Training and serving disagree about case, Unicode composition, whitespace, or control characters, so familiar text reaches different merges.

pairs.label: ID remapping
pairs.detail: A rebuilt vocabulary assigns an old piece a new integer.
pairs.explanation: A rebuilt vocabulary assigns an old piece a new integer. The model silently reads a different embedding row even when logs show recognizable token strings.

pairs.label: Narrow-corpus memorization
pairs.detail: Vocabulary capacity is spent on repeated templates or domain strings while protected traffic remains fragmented.
pairs.explanation: Vocabulary capacity is spent on repeated templates or domain strings while protected traffic remains fragmented.
